predictions.reasoning: A shift in the implied probability of a specific individual (Andy Beshear) winning the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination is a very long-dated, low-salience political signal roughly three years before the event. Nomination outcomes have no near-term policy consequence, and Beshear is not associated with a distinctive, market-moving policy platform that would differentiate him from other Democratic contenders in a way traders would price today. There is no plausible mechanism by which this probability moving over a 12-hour window transmits to broad equities. The mapping is essentially noise.

evidence_used: Market question concerns the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, ~3 years forward
Resolution depends on party nomination outcome, not immediate policy
No specified category and only 'elections' topic; no direct corporate or commodity linkage
Andy Beshear (Kentucky governor) has no uniquely market-defining policy signature relative to peers
uncertainty_notes: Long-dated nomination odds rarely move liquid assets; any correlation would be spurious
If a specific policy-linked narrative (e.g., healthcare, coal/energy given Kentucky) attached to a Beshear surge, a niche sector proxy could theoretically react, but exposure is weak and speculative
Prediction markets on distant nominations are thin and prone to noise, further weakening any signal

llm_justification.summary: This market asks whether Andy Beshear wins the 2028 Democratic nomination — a distant, low-salience political outcome with no clear near-term transmission to liquid public markets. Even a sharp implied-probability move should produce no measurable 12-hour asset response. The single mapping to broad US equities is deliberately marked unclear with very low confidence and a near-zero expected move, well below the 700bps tradable threshold.
key_assumptions: Nomination probability three years out carries no priced-in near-term policy or macro consequence
Beshear lacks a distinctive market-moving platform that traders would differentiate today
Broad equities are the only remotely relevant proxy, and even that link is negligible
failure_modes: The probability move was already public/priced and reflects nothing new
The chosen proxy (SPY) has essentially no exposure to a single candidate's nomination odds — weak proxy
A candidate-specific policy narrative could route to a niche sector we did not select, but such a move would still be small and hard to attribute
Thin prediction-market liquidity means the probability shift may be noise, not information leakage
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
